audit.whatIsWrong: Four places attribute Nasus's life steal to his ultimate: spikes[3] 'his R lifesteal outheals your Devour damage window', content.mid 'his R gives him a temporary lifesteal-and-size spike', content.late 'his R lifesteal lets him outheal your grey-health recovery', whys[4] 'a brief lifesteal-size spike'.
audit.why: Life steal is Soul Eater, his passive — it is on from level 1 and never goes away. Fury of the Sands grants bonus health, attack range, a max-health burn aura, a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown, and bonus armour and magic resist. Waiting out the ult to escape his healing is waiting for something that will not stop.
audit.corrected: Soul Eater's drain is permanent. What the ult adds is resistances, size, a faster Siphoning Strike, and an aura that burns max health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json P Soul Eater, R Fury of the Sands

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere warns that Fury of the Sands scales off the health Tahm Kench is built to stack.
audit.why: The ult damages nearby enemies for a share of max health, and Tahm Kench's core item is Heartsteel. Every stack he banks makes Nasus's ult hit him harder, and armour does not reduce it. This is the one build-level trap in the matchup and the missing-interactions file flags it as resistances-invalidated.
audit.corrected: Fury of the Sands burns a share of your max health — the more Heartsteel you stack, the more it takes, and raw armour is the wrong answer to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The range asymmetry that defines the early lane is described qualitatively ('Tongue Lash's range and slow') but never with numbers.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 900. Siphoning Strike is 255 and Wither is 700. At max Tongue Lash range Nasus cannot answer with anything at all — not even Wither. That is a positional rule the player can actually execute, rather than a vague instruction to poke.
audit.corrected: Poke from 900. Inside 700 he can Wither you; inside 255 he can Q you. Outside both, he has nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike being an auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: The wind-up, not the cast, is the tell — and Fury of the Sands cuts the Siphoning Strike cooldown further, so during the ult he resets far more often than the 3.5s rank-5 number suggests.
audit.corrected: Siphoning Strike resets his auto; read the wind-up. Under the ult it comes back faster still.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json Q flags autoReset, R description

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and wants.you[1] present 'stun into Devour' as one action.
audit.why: Tongue Lash on a three-stack target stuns and consumes the stacks; Devour on an enemy champion requires three stacks. They are alternatives.
audit.corrected: Spend three stacks on the Q-stun or on Devour, not both.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole entry is built on 'bait the Wither' but never says how long the window lasts. whys[3] instead leans on an unverified magnitude claim ('Wither can half your movement speed').
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s. That is the length of the window the entry keeps telling the player to wait for, and it is far more useful than a slow percentage the kit file does not state.
audit.corrected: Wither 15s at rank 1, 700 range. Fury of the Sands 120/100/80s. Spirit Fire 12s flat. Siphoning Strike 7.5s down to 3.5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says 'At level 6 your Abyssal Voyage adds global utility'.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate and is not in the current kit. Level 6 gives Devour.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour, not a map tool.

audit.why: Chart reads Tahm Kench 2 / Skill 4 / Nasus 1 at 56.3% over 682 games — early dominance decaying into a late-game Nasus threat, which matches the prose. No contradiction flagged in the packet and none found. The full layer's verdict of EVEN is arguably understated for 56.3%, but `diff` is shared boilerplate that occurs 27 times in the file and cannot be targeted uniquely, so I left it and report[14].t consistent with each other rather than splitting them.
content.early is accurate and well-aimed — levels 1-2 Nasus genuinely has no answer, and 'that fear compounds every wave he misses' is the right frame. Left untouched.

edits.before: Tongue Lash's range and slow lets you contest his Q last-hits immediately — Nasus has no answer to your poke before stacks matter.
edits.after: Tongue Lash reaches 900; Siphoning Strike reaches 255 and Wither 700 — poke his last-hits from outside everything Nasus owns.

edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online: spend them on the Q-stun or on Devour, not both — either burns a full stack-farm cycle.

edits.after: At 300+ Q stacks Spirit Fire's shred plus Wither cripples your chase, and Fury of the Sands piles resistances on top of Soul Eater's drain.

edits.before: Devour him off the wave whenever he steps up to Q last-hit, burning his stack-farm time
edits.after: Devour him off the wave when he steps up to Q last-hit — three stacks on him first

edits.before: Stack into his R power spike and survive lane to become the unkillable drain-fighter you cannot one-shot late
edits.after: Reach Fury of the Sands, whose aura burns a share of your max health — every Heartsteel stack feeds it

edits.before: Wither can half your movement speed and shut your chase window — neither of you can decisively kill the other, making every trade a skill read on the Wither timing.
edits.after: Wither is 15s at rank 1 and reaches only 700, so at max Tongue Lash range he cannot even cast it — every trade is a read on whether you are inside his 700 or outside it.

edits.before: His R gives him a brief lifesteal-size spike that makes short trades riskier; sit on your stacks and look for the Devour after his R timer runs down.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands adds health, range, resistances and a max-health burn while cutting his Q cooldown; sit on your stacks and commit once its 120s is spent.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where you shift from bully to controller. Your 3-stack stun is fully online and Nasus still has no real combat tool beyond Wither, but you must respect that Wither's attack and movement speed reduction can delay your gap-close just long enough for him to disengage. Bait the Wither cast first — step up, let him panic-cast it, then back off, wait for it to fall, and re-engage for the stun-Devour. At level 6 your Abyssal Voyage adds global utility but his R gives him a temporary lifesteal-and-size spike that makes short trades riskier; play for the Devour combo window rather than raw sustained fighting.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where you shift from bully to controller. Your 3-stack stun is fully online and Nasus still has no real combat tool beyond Wither, but you must respect that Wither's attack and movement speed reduction can delay your gap-close just long enough for him to disengage. Bait the Wither cast first — step up inside 700, let him panic-cast it, back off, wait out its 15 seconds, and re-engage. At level 6 you get Devour, not a map tool, while Fury of the Sands hands him health, resistances and a faster Siphoning Strike — wait out its duration instead of trading into it.

edits.before: At 2+ items and 300+ Q stacks, Nasus becomes a genuine problem: Spirit Fire shreds your armor, Wither reduces you to a crawl so you cannot reliably land the 3-stack combo without burning Flash, and his R lifesteal lets him outheal your grey-health recovery window. Your job is no longer to kill him — it is to Devour him off your carries in teamfights, buying time for your team to blow through his team while he is inside your belly. The lane is won; do not let him recover the game by fighting him alone late.
edits.after: At 2+ items and 300+ Q stacks, Nasus becomes a genuine problem: Spirit Fire shreds your armor, Wither reduces you to a crawl so you cannot reliably land the 3-stack combo without burning Flash, and Soul Eater's permanent drain outlasts your grey-health recovery. Worse, Fury of the Sands burns a share of your max health, so every Heartsteel stack you bank hands it more to work with. Devour him off your carries rather than duelling him; the lane is won, do not hand the game back late.

notes: The life-steal misattribution here is worth a champion-wide grep: Nasus's drain is Soul Eater (P), not Fury of the Sands (R), and four separate strings in this one matchup told the player to wait out the ult to escape healing that never stops. The 'Abyssal Voyage' problem reported in tahmkench__mel.json also affects this entry (content.mid). I left whys[3]'s original 'half your movement speed' claim out of the rewrite rather than restating it — the kit file gives no Wither slow magnitude, so I replaced it with the cooldown and range, which are stated. wants.foe[1] still contains 'halve your movement speed'; I left that one alone since I had nothing verified to replace it with. No WKM_LINES errors observed for this matchup.
